segments: The 11th period.
The Hunnic (Mongol) Kings.
were seeking Ahmad.
And they pursued after him,
and they overtook him near Zamm, seized him, bound him, and guarded him carefully;
and they plundered the camp of his mother and his wives.
Then Arghun and the rest of the royal princes arrived,
and they all agreed together
that Arghun should stand at the head of the Mongols,
and that he should take the kingdom in the place of Abaqa his father,
and that Ahmad should be deposed,
because he was not competent to govern.
And while the armies of the Tatars were preoccupied with fighting against each other,
Alfi (al-Alfi/Qalawun), the ruler of Egypt, sent the general Haydar,
and with him three thousand horsemen,
to the country of Shabakhtan,
to capture Bar Shakkan (Ishkhan), the Armenian general and champion,
and to bring him alive to Egypt in a cage,
because he was causing evils to the Arabs who were going to Syria.
And when they crossed the Euphrates,
they came and encamped against Tila (or Tina), a fortress belonging to the Armenians.
On the very first day that they waged battle,
he was struck by an arrow and died.
And his forces were thrown into confusion,
and they abandoned the fortress,
and fled to Syria.
And divine justice was avenged upon Haydar,
he who had continually raided the Christians,
and used to take captives and devastate the country of Melitene and Claudia (Hisn Ziyad).
These things happened in the days of summer,
in the year 1595
of the Greeks.

Now when such an end as we have mentioned came to the kingdom of Ahmad,
on Wednesday, the first of the fifth month of the Arabs,
in the year 683 [AH],
that is, on the twenty-sixth of Tammuz in the year 1595
of the Greeks
(1284 of our Lord):
Arghun, King of Kings, sat upon the throne of the kingdom.
And while many of the nobles were saying
that Ahmad ought not to live,
Arghun said,
"I will have no share in his killing.
Rather, the mother of Qonqortai and his sons know [what to do]:
if they wish, let them kill him,
and if they wish, let them let him live."
And after he had remained for some days under guard,
the sons of Qonqortai killed him,
and took vengeance for their father,
on Wednesday, the second of the sixth month of the Arabs,
that is, on the sixteenth of Ab of that same year.
And the kingdom was established for Arghun,
and he appointed each one of the royal princes over one of the countries.
